reasoning_traces.think:
The concept of profit as unimputable income establishes a foundational duality: income is either contractual (wage) or residual (profit). This distinction enables a formal decomposition of organizational returns into explicit and implicit components. Organizational control is modeled as a centralizing mechanism that aggregates individual resource contributions into a unified decision framework. Decisional risk emerges as the operational condition where control is meaningful only when tied to outcome assumption. These primitives form a triadic structure: wage-based income, control-based coordination, and risk-based profit. The failure mode occurs when control is misaligned with risk assumption, leading to mispricing of organizational returns. In GSI, this manifests as Bayesian overconfidence in residual return models. In GSE, it leads to state-space explosion due to unmodeled risk in control policies.
